name: AbBiBench
description: A benchmark that evaluates computational models of antibody binding affinity without task-specific training or fine-tuning, treating the antibody-antigen complex as the evaluation unit, using experimental measurements from 16 assays.

limitations: Coverage is broad but unbalanced. Five enrichment assays with 39,334 observations (18.2%). AlphaFold 3-predicted templates were used for the five SARS-CoV-2 assays. The ELISA readout is endpoint OD450. Direct-Kd assay counts are 10 for top-k and eight for discard.

attributes.source_locator: description: arXiv abstract and the 'we introduce AbBiBench' paragraph in the Introduction; task: Methods 3.1 (zero-shot affinity ranking); Section 1.2 and Findings 1 and 3 (Spearman equal-assay mean, top-k precision, discard precision at 30% budget); Figure 4 caption (discard-based filtering); scope_note: Section 1.1: 216,560 observations, 16 assays, 13 antibodies, nine antigen targets, eight public studies
attributes.task: Zero-shot ranking of antibody variants by predicted binding affinity to an antigen, scored on the full antibody-antigen complex. Metrics: Spearman correlation (equal-assay mean), top-k precision, and discard-based filtering (discard precision at a 30% budget).
